diagnostics.message: The explicit `depends_on = [null_resource.wait_for_cluster]` on `helm_release.karpenter` is redundant: the helm provider configuration already references `data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster` and `data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster`, both of which carry an explicit `depends_on = [null_resource.wait_for_cluster]`, so `helm_release.karpenter` already transitively waits for the cluster to become active through the provider-configuration dependency chain.

`helm_release.karpenter` deploys the Karpenter controller, whose pods can only be scheduled on cluster worker nodes. The self-managed node group (`module.self_managed_node_group`) is the source of those nodes, but nothing orders the node group before the helm release — the existing `depends_on` on `null_resource.wait_for_cluster` only guarantees the control plane is active. Since the release is installed with `wait = false`, Terraform can finish while the controller sits Pending until nodes (much later) join the cluster. The release should be ordered after the node group.

Karpenter authenticates via the Pod Identity Association created by `module.karpenter` (`create_pod_identity_association = true`), which only functions if the EKS Pod Identity Agent addon is running. `aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent` is ordered after the node group and has no path feeding into `helm_release.karpenter`, so the controller can be deployed (and start assuming roles) before the agent addon exists, causing credential failures that only self-heal once the addon lands. The helm release should depend on the addon.
